parsedVerdict.reasoning: BorrowBookUseCase.ts handles application-layer orchestration: it loads aggregates through repository interfaces and turns missing ones into not-found errors. Eligibility rules are left to the domain service LoanPolicy.assertCanBorrow, and state changes to the domain entities (book.checkOut, Loan.open). It saves through repository abstractions and gets time and IDs through application ports (Clock, IdGenerator). It maps the result to a DTO. The file has no persistence code, transport/HTTP handling or framework logic, and it does not compute business rules itself. One borderline item: the STANDARD_PERIOD constant (21 days) puts a loan-duration value in the application layer. It could arguably live in LoanPolicy, but I read it as the use case choosing a setting for a domain value object, not as embedded business logic, so it is not counted as a violation.
